business.description: W.S. Industries (India) Limited is transitioning from EPC projects into three high-growth verticals: Real Estate (residential, commercial, mixed-use, integrated townships), IT Infrastructure (data centres, technology parks, managed office ecosystems, digital infrastructure), and Warehousing & Logistics (Grade-A warehousing parks, logistics hubs, industrial infrastructure).

outlook.statement: The coming decade presents a remarkable opportunity for India. Economic growth, urbanization, digitization, and infrastructure expansion are expected to reshape industries and create new avenues for business leadership. Our Company is uniquely positioned at the intersection of three high-growth sectors—Real Estate, IT Infrastructure, and Warehousing & Logistics. Together, these businesses create a diversified growth platform capable of delivering sustainable earnings, strong cash flows, and long-term value creation.

Over the coming years, we intend to significantly enhance our project pipeline through strategic land acquisitions, joint development agreements, and partnerships with landowners. We see particular opportunities in high-growth urban corridors and emerging suburban markets where infrastructure investments are driving demand.
We are positioning ourselves to participate meaningfully in this growth story through strategic investments and partnerships.
Our plans include the development of strategically located warehousing parks, logistics hubs, and industrial infrastructure assets near key transportation corridors and consumption centres.
The proposed arrangements are expected to facilitate operational efficiency, cost-effectiveness, resource optimisation and scalability of the Company's business operations.
The proposed borrowing arrangements are expected to provide financial flexibility, facilitate timely deployment of funds for project execution and working capital requirements.

The Management expects that improvement in the order book, timely execution of projects, efficient utilisation of resources and continued cost optimization measures will contribute to improved productivity and profitability in the ensuing financial years.
The Company will be taking all effective steps to complete the pending infrastructure projects without much extension of time to realise the revenue and profitability.

Based on the objects of preferential issue your Company is pursuing all efforts for acquisition and development of further land parcels. The major activity of readying the land parcel already required have already begun.
As explained in the earlier reports your Company's business objective include development of warehousing, Data Centers, Residential, Industrial, housing and IT/ITES Facilities.

Further, the Joint Venture undertaken by the Subsidiary Company, M/s. WSI Falcon Infra Projects Private Limited, with the Prestige Group witnessed progress during the year under review with various preliminary development activities, planning exercises, and regulatory processes being undertaken. The project is presently awaiting certain key statutory and regulatory approvals for further implementation.

The Company will concentrate in the real estate sector including IT infrastructure, warehousing and Logistics, and residential and commercial ventures to create a diversified growth platform capable of delivering sustainable earnings, strong cash flows and long-term value creation.

Office leasing activity is projected to remain robust with net absorption at very high levels; retail revolution with new supply boom; residential boom with new launches exceeding 3 lakh units; logistics and industrial leasing to increase for fourth consecutive year; data center colocation capacity to rise multi-fold; institutional investments to remain benign with REITs outperforming.

The Board of Directors, at its meeting held on 26th May, 2026, approved the termination of the existing lease arrangement and sale/transfer of the Company's industrial land situated near Bengaluru to M/s. Aarnav Business Park for a consideration of not less than Rs 6.04 Crores, together with settlement of related obligations arising therefrom.

Management expects that around 90% - 95% of the transaction price allocated to unsatisfied contracts as of 31st March 2025 will be recognised as revenue during next reporting period depending upon the progress on each contracts. The remaining amounts are expected to be recognised over the next immediate year.

auditor.opinion: Unmodified opinion with Emphasis of Matter
qualifications_or_emphasis: Write-back of Payables to Overseas Customers / Suppliers aggregating to Rs 5.55 Crores pertaining to erstwhile Electro-Porcelain Products Division.
Budgetary Controls for Construction Contracts - strengthening control-based budgetary processes.

Emphasis of Matter: Note No. 34 - Amount payable to overseas customers/suppliers aggregating to Rs 5.55 crores written back during earlier years pertains to erstwhile Electro-porcelain products division (since discontinued) and management is in process of obtaining necessary approvals. Impact not ascertainable.

Emphasis of Matter: Note No. 49 - Company engaged in implementation of construction contracts with cost budgets as management estimates. Current process for arriving at project outcomes may be susceptible for deviations. Impact ascertainable only upon completion of projects.

Emphasis of Matter (a): Note No.34 to consolidated Ind AS financial statements - amount payable to overseas customers/suppliers aggregating to ` 5.55 crores written back during earlier years pertains to erstwhile Electro-porcelain products division (since discontinued) and management is in process of obtaining necessary approvals from competent authorities. Impact if any arising on account of such write back pending approvals is not ascertainable.

Emphasis of Matter (b): Note No.49 - Holding company engaged in implementation of construction contracts with cost budgets as management estimates. Current process for arriving at project outcomes may be susceptible for deviations and impact if any arising therefrom will be ascertainable only upon completion of projects, hence no adjustments made in financial statements.

CARO qualifications: Subsidiary WSI Falcon Infra Projects Private Limited - Clause xvii (Cash losses during current year). Subsidiary WSI-P&C Verticals Private Limited - Clause xvii (Cash losses during current year).
key_audit_matters: Recognition of Contract Revenue - Construction cost estimation for recognition of Rs 91.30 crore as contract revenue from fixed-price contracts recognizing revenue based on proportion of costs incurred

Related Party Transaction - Operational activities exclusively conducted through contracts with related parties involving back-to-back subcontracting, financing, material procurement, and equipment hiring requiring significant judgment on arm's length pricing

Recognition of Contract Revenue: Construction cost estimation identified as key audit matter for recognition of ` 91.30 crore as contract revenue. Since 1-2 year fixed-price contracts recognize revenue based on proportion of costs incurred, accuracy depends heavily on management's ongoing cost assessments including evaluation of potential variance claims.

Related Party Transaction: During the audit year, the Company's operational activities were exclusively conducted through contracts with related parties involving back-to-back subcontracting, financing, material procurement, and equipment hiring. Measurement and disclosure of these transactions identified as key audit matter due to significant judgment required for "arm's length" nature and inherent risk of pricing manipulation.

Amount payable to overseas customers/suppliers aggregating to ` 5.55 crores written back during earlier years pertains to erstwhile Electro-porcelain products division (since discontinued) and management is in the process of obtaining necessary approvals from competent authorities. The impact if any arising on account of such write back of amounts pending approvals is not ascertainable at this point of time.

The holding company is engaged in implementation of construction contracts, which envisage maintenance of cost budgets associated with the implementation of projects which are prepared and periodically reviewed. Though the cost budgets and revisions are management estimates, this process envisages implementation of control based budgetary process, pending which the current process for arriving at the project outcomes which may be susceptible for deviations and the impact if any arising therefrom, will be ascertainable only upon completion of the projects, hence no adjustments have been made in the financial statements.

Related party transactions: operational activities were exclusively conducted through contracts with related parties involving back-to-back subcontracting where related parties act as principal contractors. Additionally, the Company engaged in financing, material procurement, and equipment hiring from these entities. The "arm's length" nature of such exclusive arrangements requires significant judgment and carries an inherent risk of pricing manipulation that could impact the Company's profitability and financial position.
Subsidiary companies WSI Falcon Infra Projects Private Limited and WSI-P&C Verticals Private Limited reported cash losses during the current year (CARO Clause xvii).
Concentration of credit risk with respect to trade receivables is low, due to the Company's customer base primarily limited to government and other group entities.
Actual project costs and outcomes may differ from estimates owing to inherent uncertainties associated with long-term construction contracts.
